settings.title: Installing decking on pedestals
settings.text: A level, raised deck over concrete, paving or a flat roof. Here’s how the system fits together, and how to install it step by step.

settings.title: Composite decking boards
settings.text: Twin Deck boards, 4 m long, fixed to the joists with starter clips and hidden fasteners. Each board is 22 mm thick.

settings.title: Joists or subframe
settings.text: Approved aluminium or composite joists, laid at right angles to the boards and joined into a rigid frame.

settings.title: Adjustable pedestals
settings.text: Height-adjustable supports under each joist, set to the height you need.

settings.title: Protection layer
settings.text: Protective pads under each pedestal where needed, for example on a roof membrane.

settings.title: Existing base
settings.text: Sound concrete, paving or a flat roof that can carry the finished deck and drain freely.

settings.warn_text: Never lay composite boards straight onto pedestals unless the board maker has approved that exact set-up. Boards sit on joists, and the joists sit on the pedestals.
settings.title: What goes into a pedestal deck
settings.text: A pedestal deck is built in layers. The boards never touch the pedestals: they’re fixed to a frame of joists, and the frame sits on the pedestals.
settings.diagram_label: Section through a pedestal deck. From the top: decking boards 22 mm, a 50 mm joist, adjustable pedestals 78 mm tall, protection pads, and the existing base.
settings.layer_3_spec: Set to the height you need
settings.caption_left: Section through a pedestal deck · not to scale

settings.title: Work out your pedestal height
settings.text: Measure from the base to where you want the top of the deck. Take away the board and the joist, and what’s left is the height your pedestals need to reach.
settings.board_note: Twin Deck boards are 22 mm thick
settings.note_ok: Choose pedestals that adjust to around this height. Vertex pedestal sizes listed so far: 38 to 65 mm, 60 to 87 mm and 83 to 133 mm [CONFIRM].
settings.note_low: Very low. The smallest Vertex pedestal listed so far starts at 38 mm [CONFIRM], so check your pedestals or use a slimmer joist.
settings.note_none: There isn’t enough height. The board and joist alone are deeper than the space you have.
settings.count_note: Based on around 6 to 7 per m² [CONFIRM FOR THE VERTEX SYSTEM]. The real number depends on your joists, pedestal grid, deck height and loading.
settings.footnote: Example only. Allow for clips, brackets and any other parts in your system, and for any fall you need for drainage.

settings.alt: Installer building an aluminium deck frame on pedestals on a flat roof
settings.label: Before you start
settings.title: Check the base
settings.points:
Make sure the concrete or existing surface is sound and strong enough to carry the finished deck.
Check that water can drain away, and that no drainage outlets will be blocked.
On a flat roof, inspect the waterproofing and check the roof structure can take the extra load.
On a waterproof membrane, use protective pads under every pedestal. Never pierce the membrane without an approved detail.

settings.alt: Tape measure showing the height of decking boards on adjustable pedestals
settings.label: Measure
settings.title: Work out the finished height
settings.points:
Measure from the base to where you want the top of the deck.
Take away the board thickness and the joist depth. What’s left is the height your pedestals need to reach.
settings.table:
Total height available | 150 mm
Composite board | 22 mm
Joist | 50 mm
Pedestal height needed | 78 mm
settings.note: Example only. Allow for clips, brackets and any other parts in your system, or try the height calculator above.

settings.alt: Rows of adjustable pedestals under joists on a concrete base
settings.label: Set out
settings.title: Set out the pedestals
settings.points:
Mark the joist positions on the base.
Place a pedestal under each joist, at the spacing given on the Vertex data sheet.
Add extra supports at joist ends, frame junctions and wherever board ends meet.
Adjust the pedestal heads to your planned height.
settings.table:
Distance between joists | [CONFIRM: Vertex joist centres]
Maximum gap between pedestals | [CONFIRM: by joist size]
settings.note: Spacings vary a lot between systems, so always use the figures for the boards and joists you’re fitting.

settings.alt: Aluminium joists sitting in adjustable pedestals, with boards clipped on top
settings.label: Frame
settings.title: Fit the joists
settings.points:
Lay approved aluminium or composite joists into the pedestal heads, at right angles to the way the boards will run.
Fix the joists into the pedestal brackets with the specified fixings.
Join them into a rigid frame, with support around the edge and cross-bracing where needed.
Support every joint in the joists.
Avoid ordinary timber joists unless the pedestal system and site conditions allow them.

settings.alt: Checking a deck frame on pedestals with a long spirit level
settings.label: Level
settings.title: Check levels and drainage
settings.points:
Check the whole frame with a long spirit level or a laser.
Adjust each pedestal to get the finished surface you need. The frame may need a slight fall for drainage rather than being perfectly flat.
Make sure nothing rocks, every pedestal head is properly engaged, and there’s enough clearance at doors and thresholds.
settings.photo_text: Photograph the frame, joist spacing, pedestals and fixings before any boards go down. You’ll need these photos to register your warranty.

settings.alt: Fixing a hidden clip to an aluminium joist on a pedestal
settings.label: Boards
settings.title: Fit the boards
settings.points:
Fit SSL starter clips along the starting edge.
Lay the first board straight and fix it in place.
Fit the rest of the boards with the hidden clips or approved screws.
Leave the expansion gaps given on the data sheet at board ends and edges. [CONFIRM: gap sizes]
Where board ends meet, use doubled joists or a separate support for each end.
Don’t let boards overhang the frame by more than [CONFIRM: maximum overhang].

settings.alt: Finished grey composite deck with matching trims around the edge
settings.label: Finish
settings.title: Finish and inspect
settings.points:
Fit fascia boards and L-corner trims without blocking ventilation or drainage.
Check that every pedestal base is fully supported.
Check the frame for movement, loose connections and uneven areas.
Make sure roof outlets, access points and inspection covers can still be reached.
If the deck is raised or exposed to strong winds, make sure the design includes wind-uplift restraint.
settings.photo_text: Take wide shots of the whole area and close-ups of the boards and trims. These complete your warranty registration.

settings.text: Read all seven before you start. Spacings and gaps come from the Vertex data sheet for the boards and joists you’re using.
